entries.example: She bought an attractive old piece of furniture at the auction sale.
How many pieces of luggage have you got with you?
The police collected bits of information from different sources.
Today's weather has been variable. In the north there were heavy showers (of rain).

The sunny spell (of weather) that we have had this last week has continued in much of the south although there were occasional rumbles of thunder and flashes of lightning in some areas with some quite loud claps of thunder in one or two areas.
'I need a loaf of bread, a couple of slices of ham, two bars of chocolate, a tube of toothpaste, two cartons of milk and three bars of soap.'

The donkey is the basic means of transport on the island.
Tights must be the most useful article/item of clothing ever invented.
There was an interesting item of news about France on TV last night.

The nouns used with state are usually abstract and include chaos, emergency, tension, confusion, health, disorder, uncertainty, poverty, agitation, disrepair and flux [continuous change], e.g. a state of emergency.

note: Presentation is prose with bold collocation phrases; no printed definitions, POS markers, IPA or sense numbers exist. Entries are bold phrases with their first printed example sentence where one exists; group = section heading (Weather/Groceries/Nature/Other). Exercises page not extracted.
